curiosities: Philips made three Zelda games and Hotel Mario for it under a deal with Nintendo.
It was sold as a multimedia player for education and entertainment rather than as a games console.
A Digital Video Cartridge added MPEG-1 decoding for Video CD films.
It ran CD-RTOS, a version of Microware's OS-9.
It launched in the US in December 1991.
Philips developed the CD-i standard with Sony.
The CD-i 450 of 1994 was a cheaper model aimed at games.
Its remote-style controller has a thumb pad for steering a pointer.
Burn:Cycle of 1994 is among its best-known games.
